programme.name: Human Development and Aging, Honors Programs (BS)

unit_statements_verbatim:
Honors Program (Minimum 10 units):
GERO 497a , GERO 497b , GERO 497c and GERO 593
All honors courses may be applied toward the required upper-division gerontology elective units.
Students begin in the fall or spring of junior year with 2 units of GERO 497a as they start developing their honors thesis.
In the second semester, they take 2 units of GERO 497b as they finalize their research design and begin the project.
Students complete GERO 593 (4 units, minimum grade of B) during the first or second semester in the program.
In the third semester, students take 2–4 units of GERO 497c with the goal of completing the research and writing the thesis.

- GERO 200 Gerontology: The Science of Adult Development Units: 4
- GERO 320g Psychology of Adult Development Units: 4
- GERO 330 Society and Adult Development Units: 4
- GERO 340 Policy, Values, and Power in an Aging Society Units: 4
- GERO 416 Health Issues in Adulthood Units: 4
- GERO 470 Aging and Business Units: 4
- GERO 491 Practicum Units: 2-8
- GERO 492 Senior Seminar Units: 4
- General Education Units: 24
- Writing Requirement Units: 8
- Foreign Language or Programming Units: 12
- Gerontology Elective Units: 8-10
- One approved statistics course Units: 4
- General electives in gerontology or related disciplines (8 units upper division) Units: 32

### Gerontology Honors Courses

---

- GERO 497a Honors Seminar Units: 2 [*]
- GERO 497b Honors Seminar Units: 2 [*]
- GERO 497c Honors Seminar Units: 2-4 [*]
- GERO 593 Research Methods Units: 4

## Total units: 128

notes.text: USC Davis offers an honors program to outstanding students pursuing the BS in Human Development and Aging. The program gives students the chance to work on mentored undergraduate research, take coursework in research methods and statistics in aging, and complete an honors thesis. Students who finish the program earn the designation of Bachelor of Science in Human Development and Aging with Honors on their transcript.

notes.text: Eligibility: Students must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.3 and a minimum 3.5 GPA in GERO courses. For Health Science Track students, only GERO courses offered by the School of Gerontology count toward the GERO GPA requirement. To graduate with Honors, students must also finish the program with at least a 3.3 cumulative GPA and a 3.5 GERO GPA.
